c153.title: New neighbors
c153.story: A family of [[immigrants|immigrant]] moved into Anna's building last week. Their son lives in America and just got his [[green card]]. Last month, their daughter Lina visited the [[consulate]], where the [[consul]] helped her with papers. Lina told Anna about [[racism]] at her old school and a [[racist]] neighbor there. Before Kyiv, the family lived in a poor [[ghetto]] in a big, noisy city. Now her parents work hard and hope to join the [[middle class]] here. Anna's grandpa was born during the [[baby boom]], so he is a real [[baby boomer]]. Max smiled and said young people just say "[[boomer]]" for short. Grandpa calls himself a [[nationalist]], so Lina asked him what that means. They had a long, friendly argument about [[nationalism]], while Lina's brother, a [[millennial]], listened. In the end, Grandpa smiled and said, "Every [[migrant]] is welcome at my table."

c155.title: A day in parliament
c155.story: On Thursday, Anna's class visited [[parliament]], and a guide explained each party's political [[agenda]]. At a press [[briefing]], a young [[minister]] talked about schools, and the [[premier]] discussed the budget. Mr. Koval explained that some countries have a [[senate]], where each [[senator]] votes on laws. "In America, the Senate is one part of [[Congress|congress]]," he added. "The other part, the House, has hundreds of [[congressmen|congressman]] and [[congresswomen|congresswoman]]." In the hall, a [[lobbyist]] from the energy [[lobby]] waited with a thick folder. The members argued for hours but finally reached a [[compromise]]. The guide said full [[consensus]] is rare, because many people just want the [[status quo]]. Now they had a budget, so there would be no [[shutdown]] this year. Anna asked about [[impeachment]], and Mr. Koval explained it with a funny example. On the bus home, Max asked so many questions that he became the [[de facto]] guide.

c157.title: Students protest
c157.story: On Saturday, Anna and Max joined a student [[protest]] near the university. The city wanted to close the student library and build a parking lot. A young [[activist]], Sofia, said her [[activism]] began in a library like this one. "We have one [[ideal]]: free books for everyone," she said. Max liked her [[idealism]], but he did not believe in a perfect [[utopia]]. Then workers from a local [[trade union]] arrived with big signs. They promised a one-day [[strike]] and called for a [[boycott]] of the parking company. A man in a black hat said he was an [[anarchist]] and shouted at the sky. Max's friend Oleh, a real [[cynic]], called all the politicians [[hypocrites|hypocrite]]. He said the whole march was [[nonsense]]. Two weeks later, the city kept the library open, and even Oleh brought cake.

c160.title: Anna's internship at a newspaper
c160.story: In July, Anna started a month-long internship in a busy [[newsroom]]. An older [[journalist]] named Petro showed her how to check every fact. Next to him sat a [[columnist]] who was writing the Sunday [[editorial]]. At noon, a [[correspondent]] abroad called with an [[exclusive]]: a [[scandal]] at a famous football club. A [[tabloid]] already had rumors about it. "They want [[publicity]], not facts," Petro said. Meanwhile, the club's [[PR]] people kept calling to stop the story. The [[publisher]] read the morning [[digest]] and asked for a quick [[rewrite]]. He wanted the true story, not the old [[narrative]] about the club. By evening, the [[media]] waited outside the club, and a TV [[reporter]] went live. Petro let Anna write the headline. The next morning, the [[mass media]] everywhere repeated it.

c161.title: Anna's cousin in the army
c161.story: Anna's cousin Taras was a [[cadet]] only four years ago. Now he is an [[officer]], and he trains every new [[recruit]]. On Sunday, he visited Anna and told stories over tea. His [[lieutenant]] is strict but fair, and his [[sergeant]] tells terrible jokes. Last month, his [[battalion]] moved a [[convoy]] of trucks through a [[checkpoint]]. They slept in a cold [[bunker]] and wore [[camouflage]] in the forest. A small [[drone]] watched them from above, and a [[tank]] moved slowly behind. In the exercise, half of the soldiers played enemy [[combatants|combatant]]. Taras was the colonel's [[adjutant]], so he carried orders to the base [[commandant]] on foot. Grandpa laughed and said he once served under a navy [[commodore]], one step below an [[admiral]]. Asked why he joined, Taras said, "I'm a [[patriot]], and I want my family safe." Most of all, they all dream of marching in a big peace [[parade]] together.
